Lastly, the Peak Season Average Net Power is calculated as the average of the net power generated in July, August, and September when the surface water temperature is the warmest. 25 OESI 2.0 M-1 T-1-P1.1 – Objective 3 Report April 2025 It should be noted that whereas typical power systems use the peak available power production capacity as their nameplate power, the authors of this report decided to use the annual average rating for conservatism as well as to accurately reflect the impacts of seasonal water column temperature variability. Output: Major Equipment Data Based on the cold-water pipe size, the process equipment is pre-determined in the model. The Equipment Data section of the output provides information about the number of heat exchangers (condensers and evaporators) as well as their heat transfer coefficients and area. The number of turbine generators and their rating is also provided. Additional detail about the refrigerant piping sizes needed for the OTEC plant is also provided. For the CW pumping power, WW pumping power, and refrigerant pumping power, the values generated for the warmest (highest power output) are provided. Output: Process Data To provide the user perspective on the size of the equipment, the CW and WW flow rates are provided in imperial and metric units. Also, the flow rate or the refrigerant is provided in both the liquid phase and the liquid phase. In addition, the range (minimum and maximum) refrigerant temperatures and pressures are provided. Output: Real Levelized Cost of Electricity The methodology for determining the variables comprising the capital cost and operation and maintenance costs is described in detail in Appendix 4 of the Objective 2 report. In this interactive model, the LCOE is calculated using no power transmission distance since the default is that the OTEC plant will be co-located with the power demand. In addition, the initial LCOE uses the default values for system availability, interest rate, escalation rate, and system life. On the Real LCOE tab, the model enables the user to modify one or more of the default values and immediately see how those values impact the calculated LCOE. Real, rather than nominal, LCOE was chosen to be consistent with the LCOE methodology used for other technologies in the Annual Technology Baseline (ATB) from the National Renewable Energy Laboratory (NREL 2024). Additionally, whereas typical cost basis calculations consider fractions of funding comprised of debt financing and equity, the authors in this report made the simplifying assumption of 100% debt financing. Future revisions to this tool may be made to add the ability to consider an equity financing option. 26 OESI 2.0 M-1 T-1-P1.1 – Objective 3 Report April 2025 6.3 Discussion In addition to the inputs and outputs shown above, it is important to note several limitations of the hypothetical OTEC visualization tool discussed in this report.
